conversation.text: Exactly. The technical capabilities are advancing so rapidly that the legal and ethical frameworks are struggling to keep up. The sophistication of these deepfakes is becoming almost indistinguishable from reality, making it harder to detect manipulation.

conversation.text: The voice cloning technology is particularly concerning. With relatively little data, you can create a convincing imitation of someone's voice. Imagine the implications for customer service, political campaigns, or even personal relationships.

conversation.speaker: Smithi
conversation.text: Absolutely. And the Johansson case exposed the inadequacy of current legal protections. While she eventually got OpenAI to pause the voice, it highlighted the need for clearer regulations regarding voice and likeness rights in the age of AI.

conversation.speaker: Andrew Krepthy
conversation.text: It boils down to consent and control. Individuals should have the right to control how their image and voice are used, especially in AI-generated content. The current landscape is a bit of a Wild West.

conversation.speaker: Smithi

conversation.speaker: Andrew Krepthy
